default: # Antigravity Skill Vault [![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy_Me_a_Coffee-support-FFDD00?logo=buymeacoffee&logoColor=black)](https://buymeacoffee.com/rmyndharis) A curated collection of **Agent Skills** for **Google Antigravity**, ported from the [Claude Code Agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents) repository. This vault transforms the extensive Claude Code ecosystem into **Antigravity Skills**, providing your agent with repeatable workflows, domain expertise, and specialized tools. --- ## 🚀 Overview This repository contains **300+ specialized skills** across software development, operations, security, and business domains. Each skill is a directory-based package that teaches Antigravity's agent how to perform specific tasks. ### What's Included? The skills are derived from three types of Claude Code components, all unified into the Antigravity Skill format: 1. **Domain Skills** (e.g., `k8s-manifest-generator`, `async-python-patterns`): Specialized knowledge packages. 2. **Specialist Agents** (e.g., `backend-architect`, `security-auditor`): Persona-based instruction sets for complex reasoning. 3. **Commands & Workflows** (e.g., `full-stack-orchestration-full-stack-feature`, `conductor-implement`): Structured, multi-step procedures. --- ## 📂 Categories Skills are flattened in the `skills/` directory, but cover these broad categories: ### 💻 Development & Languages - **Python**: `python-pro`, `fastapi-pro`, `async-python-patterns`, `uv-package-manager` - **JavaScript/TypeScript**: `typescript-pro`, `react-modernization`, `nextjs-app-router-patterns` - **Systems**: `rust-pro`, `golang-pro`, `memory-safety-patterns` - **Mobile**: `frontend-mobile-development-component-scaffold`, `react-native-architecture` ### ☁️ Infrastructure & Operations - **Kubernetes**: `kubernetes-architect`, `helm-chart-scaffolding`, `gitops-workflow` - **Cloud**: `cloud-architect`, `terraform-module-library`, `cost-optimization` - **CI/CD**: `cicd-automation-workflow-automate`, `github-actions-templates`, `gitlab-ci-patterns` ### 🔒 Security & Quality - **Security**: `security-auditor`, `sast-configuration`, `security-scanning-security-hardening` - **Code Quality**: `code-review-ai-ai-review`, `code-refactoring-refactor-clean`, `codebase-cleanup-tech-debt` - **Testing**: `unit-testing-test-generate`, `tdd-workflows-tdd-cycle`, `e2e-testing-patterns` ### 🔄 Workflows & Architecture - **Conductor**: `conductor-implement`, `context-driven-development` (Context-Driven Development) - **Architecture**: `c4-architecture-c4-architecture`, `microservices-patterns`, `api-design-principles` - **Orchestration**: `full-stack-orchestration-full-stack-feature`, `incident-response-incident-response` ### 📊 Data & AI - **Data Engineering**: `data-engineer`, `spark-optimization`, `dbt-transformation-patterns` - **AI/ML**: `ml-pipeline-workflow`, `prompt-engineering-patterns`, `rag-implementation` --- ## 🎯 Install Strategically (Token Efficient) Antigravity loads metadata (name + description) from every installed skill at session start. More skills means more token usage and a higher chance of irrelevant auto-activation. Prefer targeted installs via search, tags, or bundles. `install --all` is advanced and not recommended for most projects. ## 🧭 Catalog & Discovery This repo ships a generated catalog for discovery: - `CATALOG.md` (human-readable index) - `catalog.json` (machine-readable index used by the CLI) - `bundles.json` (curated bundles) - `aliases.json` (short names that map to long skill IDs) Regenerate after adding/editing skills. This also synchronizes the manager skill into the dedicated plugin package: ```bash npm run build:catalog ``` ## 🛠️ How to Use When a conversation starts, Antigravity loads the **metadata** (name & description) from all skills. ANTIGRAVITY automatically activates a skill when your request matches its description. **Examples:** * *"Help me design a REST API for a user service"* → Activates `api-design-principles` and `backend-architect`. * *"Scaffold a new FastAPI project"* → Activates `python-development-python-scaffold`. * *"Review this PR for security issues"* → Activates `security-scanning-security-hardening` or `security-auditor`. * *"Start a new feature track for login"* → Activates `conductor-new-track`. --- The npm CLI provides two default installation scopes: - **Workspace scope** (project-specific): `/.agent/skills/` - **Global scope** (`--global`): `~/.gemini/config/skills/`, read by the Antigravity App, CLI, and IDE `AG_SKILLS_DIR` overrides either destination and expands a leading `~`. Antigravity supports the CLI's `.agent/skills/` workspace path for backward compatibility; the current default is `.agents/skills/`. Earlier versions installed global skills to `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/`, which only the standalone IDE still reads; `doctor` reports that directory when it exists. See the official [skill locations](https://www.antigravity.google/docs/skills/). For example, select the current workspace convention, or manage global skills left by an earlier version: ```bash AG_SKILLS_DIR=.agents/skills npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install bash-pro AG_SKILLS_DIR="$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/skills" npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills installed ``` Use the same override with `installed`, `update`, and `doctor` when inspecting or changing that installation. ### Using `npx` (Recommended) Run the published npm CLI from your intended workspace. Node.js and npm are required; cloning this repository is optional. To add the manager skill itself: ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install antigravity-skills-manager npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills doctor npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills installed ``` Start a new Antigravity session, then invoke `/antigravity-skills-manager` followed by your request. You can also use the CLI directly without installing the manager skill. **1. Search skills (recommended first):** ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills search # Example: npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills search kubernetes ``` **2. List available skills:** ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills list ``` **3. Install a specific skill to your current project:** ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install # Example: npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install bash-pro ``` An existing skill directory is skipped. Add `--force` only to replace it, including any local edits: ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install bash-pro --force ``` **4. Install by tag or bundle (targeted sets):** ```bash # By tag npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install --tag kubernetes # By bundle npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install --bundle core-dev ``` Available bundles: `core-dev`, `security-core`, `k8s-core`, `data-core`, `ai-core`, `ops-core`. Each holds at most 10 hand-picked skills. `core-dev` is language-agnostic; add language skills by tag, for example `install --tag python`. **5. Install a skill globally:** ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install --global # Example: npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install bash-pro --global ``` **6. Check installed skills:** ```bash # List local specific skills npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills installed # List globally installed skills npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills installed --global ``` **7. Update installed skills:** ```bash # Update a specific skill npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills update # Update ALL installed skills npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills update # Update global skills npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills update --global ``` `update` and `install --force` replace each selected skill directory completely, removing files deleted upstream and discarding local edits. Back up custom changes before replacing a skill. Ordinary `install` preserves an existing directory by skipping it. Each replacement is prepared before the previous directory is moved. Copy failures preserve the existing installation; activation failures attempt to restore it. If restoration fails, the error identifies the retained backup. Interrupted installations can leave a hidden `..install-lock` and `..install-*` recovery directory beside the skill. Inspect and preserve any backup before cleanup, and remove a stale lock only after confirming that no installer is running. File or symlink destinations, source symlinks, and overlapping source/destination paths are rejected. **8. Doctor / stats:** ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills doctor npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills stats ``` **9. Install ALL skills (advanced, not recommended):** ```bash # To your current workspace npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install --all # Globally npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install --all --global ``` > **Note:** Installing all skills increases token usage and can trigger unrelated skills. Prefer targeted installs. Aliases are supported via `aliases.json` (for long skill names). Example: ```bash npx @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills install full-stack-feature ``` ### Installing the npm CLI globally To make the `ag-skills` executable available on your PATH: ```bash npm install --global @rmyndharis/antigravity-skills ag-skills install antigravity-skills-manager ``` `npm install --global` installs the executable. It does not select a global skill destination. Use `ag-skills install --global` for the global skill directory, or `AG_SKILLS_DIR` for another location. ### Using a source checkout To run unpublished checkout changes reliably, run `npm ci` in the repository root, then invoke its CLI from your intended workspace. A package-name `npx` command resolves an installed package or the published release; it does not explicitly select this checkout: ```bash node /absolute/path/to/antigravity-skills/bin/cli.js install antigravity-skills-manager node /absolute/path/to/antigravity-skills/bin/cli.js installed ``` ### Using `agy plugin install` (experimental) Local plugin installation, enable/disable, and manager invocation have been verified in the Antigravity app on macOS with `agy 1.3.3`. With an npm package packed from this checkout and installed into an isolated workspace, the manager searched the catalog, installed and listed a skill, preserved local files during an ordinary reinstall, and updated only the selected skill. These results apply to the checkout payload, not to an earlier npm release. The npm CLI can also be used independently. The dedicated plugin contains only the manager skill. Install its directory following the official [plugin installation instructions](https://www.antigravity.google/docs/plugins?tab=cli): ```bash git clone https://github.com/rmyndharis/antigravity-skills.git agy plugin validate ./antigravity-skills/plugins/antigravity-skills-manager agy plugin install ./antigravity-skills/plugins/antigravity-skills-manager ``` Do not package the repository root as a plugin. Plugin skill discovery would include the entire vault under its `skills/` directory. The root intentionally has no plugin manifest. Inspect the manager in the app's Customizations view, then invoke its displayed command: ```text /antigravity-skills-manager search flutter /antigravity-skills-manager install flutter-expert into this workspace /antigravity-skills-manager list installed skills ``` The manager uses the npm CLI commands above, so Node.js and npm must be available. The plugin does not register separate command aliases. The package contains one skill, `antigravity-skills-manager`. On `agy 1.3.3`, `agy plugin list --json` lists imported plugins without component names or enabled state; use the Customizations view to inspect activation and command discovery. ### Manual Installation If you prefer to clone the repository: **Option A — Install to a workspace** ```bash mkdir -p .agent/skills cp -R /path/to/antigravity-skills/skills/ .agent/skills/ ``` **Option B — Install globally** ```bash mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills cp -R /path/to/antigravity-skills/skills/ ~/.gemini/config/skills/ ``` > **Note:** After copying skills, restart your agent session so Antigravity re-detects them. --- ## ➕ Adding New Skills 1. Create a folder: `skills//` 2. Add `SKILL.md` (required) 3. (Optional) Add helpers: `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/` Skills must work with the files in their own directory and publicly available tools; skills that need unpublished software or a path from one machine are not accepted. Skills about a specific tool are welcome when they teach a reusable workflow, but not when their main purpose is to promote a project. ### Development checks Install the Node dependencies and Python test dependencies before running the complete checks: ```bash npm ci python3 -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python3 -m pip install -r requirements-test-assets.txt npm run build:catalog npm test npm run test:python npm run validate:skills npm run check:catalog ``` `npm run test:python` includes tests for shipped helper scripts and requires the packages in `requirements-test-assets.txt`. `npm run test:assets` runs only those helper-script tests. Activate the virtual environment before running these commands; on Windows, use `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in PowerShell. Edit the canonical manager skill at `skills/antigravity-skills-manager/SKILL.md`. `npm run build:catalog` copies it into `plugins/antigravity-skills-manager/skills/antigravity-skills-manager/SKILL.md`; `npm run check:catalog` checks that the copy is current without changing it. ### Authoring Guidelines - Keep `SKILL.md` concise; move long examples to `resources/` or `examples/`. - Use narrow descriptions (for example: "Use when you need to ...") and include "Do not use" to reduce over-activation. Validation rejects descriptions that open with "You are" or ask for "PROACTIVELY" use, and Claude Code-only syntax such as `$ARGUMENTS` or Task tool steps anywhere in a skill. - Add a "Safety" section for skills that propose terminal or infrastructure changes. - Regenerate catalog files with `npm run build:catalog`, then run `npm run prepublishOnly` for the complete local gate. CI runs the same Node, Python, validation, and catalog checks. - `npm run validate:skills` runs the same strict validation as CI, using `validation-baseline.json` for existing gaps; new skills must include the required sections outside code examples. Helper paths under `resources/`, `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, and `examples/` are checked in every Markdown file, including links and bold paths. Use paths relative to the skill directory and include the referenced files. - The baseline is intentionally empty. Refreshing it (`node scripts/validate-skills.js --write-baseline --yes`) grandfathers — and thus silences — current soft violations, so avoid it unless you truly need to; without `--yes` the command only previews what it would grandfather. ### SKILL.md Template ```markdown --- name: description: --- # ## Use this skill when - ... ## Do not use this skill when - ... ## Instructions 1. ... 2. ... ``` --- ## 🔐 Security See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for safety expectations when writing skills that touch terminals or infrastructure. --- ## ☕ Support If this vault saves you time, you can support its maintenance by buying me a coffee. --- ## 📜 License MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. Original content © [Claude Code Agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents). Ported to Antigravity Skills.

CI runs the same Node, Python, validation, and catalog checks. - `npm run validate:skills` runs the same strict validation as CI, using `validation-baseline.json` for existing gaps; new skills must include the required sections outside code examples. Helper paths under `resources/`, `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, and `examples/` are checked in every Markdown file, including links and bold paths. Use paths relative to the skill directory and include the referenced files. - The baseline is intentionally empty. Refreshing it (`node scripts/validate-skills.js --write-baseline --yes`) grandfathers — and thus silences — current soft violations, so avoid it unless you truly need to; without `--yes` the command only previews what it would grandfather. ### SKILL.md Template ```markdown --- name: description: --- # ## Use this skill when - ... ## Do not use this skill when - ... ## Instructions 1. ... 2. ... ``` --- ## 🔐 Security See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for safety expectations when writing skills that touch terminals or infrastructure. --- ## ☕ Support If this vault saves you time, you can support its maintenance by buying me a coffee. --- ## 📜 License MIT License.
